summary: Request for customer-facing “compliance report” summarizing retention controls + audit logging (what can be shared)
description:
Issue summary:
Prospect B requested a “compliance report” (PDF/packet) covering:
- Current retention posture (defaults, configurability, guardrails)
- Audit logging coverage and export options
- Evidence we can share to satisfy procurement/security review

Customer request details:
- They want a single document to attach to their security review packet (in addition to SOC 2).
- They asked for: retention durations by data type, how audit logs are protected/immutable, export format and frequency, and whether legal hold is supported.
- They specifically asked if Redwood can provide a ‘control mapping’ table (SOC2/ISO style) showing evidence artifacts.

Impact:
- Blocking security review completion. Customer indicated procurement timeline is tight (2–3 weeks).

What customer asked to receive:
1) A customer-facing summary report (ideally PDF) on retention + audit logging
2) A statement on legal holds / exceptions
3) Any available evidence or attestations we can share now

Notes:
- This overlaps with the new Compliance Reporting Pack initiative and retention controls v1 work. We need GRC approval (Olga) on what can be shared externally vs internal-only.

Requested deliverable target:
- Customer asked for EOW (by 2025-02-14) if possible; otherwise a partial packet plus a date for the full pack.

Attachments referenced by customer:
- They referenced SUP-4831 artifacts and asked for the same “report format” rather than separate links.

Support owner ask:
- Need GRC to confirm external-safe content (no internal system diagrams, no internal-only control mapping).
internal_notes:
Internal coordination needed:
- Confirm what’s approved to share externally:
  - Customer-facing compliance reporting pack v1 (sanitized) vs internal control-to-evidence mapping.
  - Whether we can share retention enforcement job details (metrics, runbook excerpts) or just behavioral commitments.
- Ensure alignment with Legal (Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes) on retention language (avoid contractual commitments beyond current product).
- If we share ‘legal hold’ concept: clearly specify v1 semantics (hold flag prevents deletion for in-scope datasets; may not apply to all infra logs).

Proposed external-safe content (draft):
- “Retention Controls Overview” (supported datasets, defaults, configurability, guardrails)
- “Audit Logging Overview” (event coverage categories, access controls, export options, retention interactions)
- “Retention & Audit Logging Attestation” (high-level statement + how customers can verify in Console once enabled)
- Optional: ‘Evidence availability table’ WITHOUT mapping to specific SOC2 CC numbers (keep it customer-friendly, avoid making it look like an auditor-ready control matrix)

Not external-safe (likely):
- Full control-to-evidence mapping with internal system names/locations
- Detailed datastore implementation specifics (table names, shard/partition schemes, internal dashboards)

Owners:
- Olga Petrov (approve external share list)
- Daniel Carter (assemble/report pack execution)
- Markus Klein / Solutions Eng (customer delivery & framing)

Tracking:
- INT-912 for standard export/zip/PDF packaging; until then, we may send a manually assembled PDF + attachments.
comments:
2025-02-10 09:18 (Dev Patel - Support Readiness)
Created ticket from SE escalation. Prospect is requesting a single ‘compliance report’ specifically on retention + audit logging. Assigning to Rachel for customer readiness + coordination.

2025-02-10 10:02 (Rachel Kim)
Acknowledged. Looping in Olga (GRC) + Daniel (pack execution) for guidance on what is approved to share externally.

2025-02-10 12:11 (Olga Petrov)
We can share: customer-facing narrative summary + an evidence availability overview (high-level). We should NOT share the internal control mapping table as-is (it includes internal evidence locations and could be misinterpreted as an auditor deliverable). If they need SOC 2 mapping, we can provide our SOC 2 report under NDA and point to the relevant sections.

2025-02-11 08:37 (Rachel Kim)
Draft plan:
1) Provide SOC 2 report under NDA (existing process)
2) Provide a customer-facing ‘Retention + Audit Logging Summary’ (2–4 pages) with:
   - Retention: supported datasets in v1 (audit logs, admin activity, selected telemetry/analytics metadata), defaults, min/max guardrails, exceptions/legal hold concept
   - Audit logs: coverage, integrity/access controls, export formats, how retention affects exports
   - Verification: what will be visible in Console (effective policy, last enforcement run) once enabled
3) Provide an appendix with export format sample (redacted)
Requesting Daniel to assemble a PDF based on the reporting pack v1 structure.

2025-02-11 14:22 (Daniel Carter)
I can assemble a customer-safe v1 packet from the reporting pack outline. Need final approval from Olga on exact wording for (a) ‘legal hold’ and (b) ‘enforcement proof’ (we can describe the controls without implying continuous audit/attestation).

2025-02-12 09:05 (Olga Petrov)
Approved language guidance:
- Avoid “guarantee” phrasing; use “designed to” and “configured to enforce.”
- For legal hold: “When enabled, retention enforcement is suspended for in-scope datasets for the tenant until hold is removed; exceptions are reviewed periodically.”
- For enforcement proof: “Console surfaces last enforcement run timestamp and status; audit events are generated for policy changes.”

2025-02-12 11:47 (Rachel Kim)
Customer comms drafted. Looping in Markus (SE) to send and contextualize in the security review.

2025-02-13 16:10 (Markus Klein)
Sent customer:
- ‘Retention & Audit Logging Summary (v1, customer-facing)’ PDF
- SOC 2 report delivery instructions (NDA gate)
- Audit log export sample (redacted)
Customer asked a follow-up: can we include a table of retention durations by dataset for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? I told them we can provide defaults + what’s configurable, and for Private it’s deployment-dependent.

2025-02-14 09:28 (Rachel Kim)
Following up with Daniel to add a one-page table (deployment mode x dataset x default retention x configurable y/n x notes/constraints). This should remain non-contractual and note that some infra logs are governed by SRE/vendor constraints.

2025-02-14 15:02 (Daniel Carter)
Updated PDF with the requested table and explicit ‘Scope notes’ section (what is in v1 vs later). Sent to Markus for delivery.

2025-02-18 10:41 (Rachel Kim)
Markus confirmed customer accepted the packet for now; they may request additional evidence once they see Console screenshots. Closing as Resolved; if they need a formal control mapping, we should route to GRC with NDA and share SOC2 report + targeted narrative responses rather than internal matrix.

Resolution:
- Delivered customer-facing retention + audit logging summary packet (sanitized)
- Provided SOC 2 report process (NDA)
- Clarified what we cannot share (internal control-to-evidence mapping)

Next steps (internal):
- INT-912: standardize exportable compliance pack zip/PDF for Sales/SE
- Update Sales enablement FAQ to reflect ‘what we can share’ guidance
resolution: Provided a customer-facing compliance packet summarizing retention controls and audit logging, plus redacted export sample and SOC 2 report delivery process under NDA. Confirmed with GRC that the internal control-to-evidence mapping is not shared externally; instead we provide a high-level evidence availability overview and SOC 2 report where applicable.
